nodes.title: JubAp.Net: An AI Development Center Built Through Operational Waves
nodes.reading:
JubAp.Net is best understood not as a conventional AI lab, but as an applied intelligence engineering center shaped by real operational constraints. Its identity was not formed in abstraction or in the current generative AI wave, but through a long progression across distributed mobility, industrial digitalization, enterprise integration, and operational AI. The result is an engineering culture that values resilience, traceability, and usefulness under pressure more than theoretical elegance.

From the beginning, the organization’s work evolved inside environments where systems had to function despite fragmented data, unstable connectivity, high coupling, and mission-critical expectations. That context shaped a very specific style of architecture: adaptive, modular, explainable, and designed to survive real-world friction.

nodes.title: Luxury Recommendation
nodes.reading:
Industrial Case · Luxury Operations · Recommendation Systems · Vector Databases · SLM Architecture · Enterprise Data

In a high-end luxury group, a recommendation engine cannot be treated as a small add-on inside SAP, Salesforce or any single application.

The problem is not merely to search for products or to show “people who bought X also bought Y”. Recommendation in this context means connecting, in real time and with high precision:

Product and reference, client and household, purchase history, repair and after-sales history, style, aesthetics and cultural context.

Events, invitations, scarcity, boutique, region, channel, collection logic, design narratives, technical documentation and training content.

nodes.title: Case Study: Rationalization in Luxury
nodes.reading:
A three-year, Steering-level programme across more than 50 Maisons — rationalizing the global application landscape to enable post-M&A integration and cross-Maison value, while preserving the heritage and identity of each house.

Enterprise architecture, rationalization & technology value creation · Stewarded by The Integral Management Society / IMSV.org

Richemont is not a conventional multinational. It is a constellation of more than 50 Maisons, legal entities, regional structures, manufacturing environments and retail networks, many with their own history, operating logic and — in some cases — centuries of accumulated organizational DNA. Over the years the Group’s balance between centralization and decentralization had shifted repeatedly, and each Maison had grown its own ecosystem of applications, local workflows and technology decisions.

The engagement began without the foundations most groups assume already exist: there was no Group-wide enterprise-architecture management system, and no consolidated multi-entity application inventory. Even the basic question — what counts as “an application”? — had to be defined before anything could be counted.

When discovery ran across every region, country and entity, an early finding was significant: the degree of duplication by capability was roughly three times higher than expected . That duplication was not always inefficiency. Much of it reflected genuine differences in customer expectations, local regulation, regional business models and Maison identity. This framed the central question of the programme:

nodes.title: El diamante tecnológico puede estar funcionando dentro de la empresa y seguir invisible
nodes.summary: ¿Por qué proponer otra plataforma antes de preguntar qué solución existente ya resolvió el problema dentro de una Maison?
nodes.reading:
INTERLOCUTOR (pregunta editorial, no necesariamente pronunciada) — ¿Por qué proponer otra plataforma antes de preguntar qué solución existente ya resolvió el problema dentro de una Maison?
REFLEXIÓN DEL DIÁLOGO (voces y estatutos señalados en origen) — En una conversación de diseño de servicio, Iván rechazó comenzar con un nuevo MVP o una tecnología que el cliente tendría que financiar para probar nuestra idea. Quería encontrar primero los «diamantes»: soluciones ya usadas, aprobadas y con resultados concretos dentro de la propia empresa. No bastaba abrir el inventario. Había que entrevistar a quienes conocen las capacidades, entender en qué contexto funcionan y revisar si se pueden replicar con cambios pequeños.

El desplazamiento es arquitectónico. Una organización compleja puede pagar varias veces por resolver la misma función porque sus unidades no conocen lo que otras ya hacen bien. El recurso raro no es siempre el software; puede ser la visibilidad de una capacidad, la confianza en sus resultados, o las condiciones que permiten transferirla sin romper dependencias.

Esta ficha complementa la crítica a la acumulación de aplicaciones, pero ofrece una dirección positiva: buscar primero valor probado internamente y después decidir sobre sustitución, integración o extensión. «Diamante» es la imagen del usuario; la formalización del método es reconstrucción editorial. Debe contrastarse cada oportunidad antes de atribuir ahorros o adopción realizada.
